claims.claim: A hand-labeled seed dataset of 48 real public repos across 5 death-modes ships in-repo (10 alive / 10 abandoned / 10 pivoted / 9 completed / 9 burned_out).
The seed CSV is built by the SAME production feature extractor; 2 repos dropped (genuine 404s), 6 recovered via the 301-redirect fix.

TabPFN LOO was UNMEASURABLE this build (Prior Labs HTTP 503 'Service is disabled'); the 1-NN proxy LOO on standardized features = 15/48 = 31% (chance 20%). Reported honestly; app ships rules-primary per ADR-007.
The core AI is open-source only: TabPFN (open weights) classifies via tabpfn-client + set_access_token; narration is Gemma (open weights) via Ollama. No closed model in the verdict/narration path.
Every verdict carries an engine flag (tabpfn|rules) surfaced verbatim on the certificate; a fallback is labeled 'forensic-rules estimate — model unavailable'.
Narration rejects any 2+-digit number absent from the evidence block (retry once, then templated fallback). The grounding test proves a fabricated 99999 is rejected.
The full local loop runs end-to-end: real repo -> features -> classify -> grounded eulogy -> AutopsyResult JSON; /healthz 200, bad input -> 422, 404 repo -> friendly 422 (no uncaught 500).
All 4 offline test suites pass (14 cases): validators, features, classifier shape, narration grounding.
A 1200x630 certificate screenshot for each of 3 example repos (abandoned / burned_out / alive) for the post cover image.
The app is live on the Oracle Always-Free VM, warm, with Gemma-via-Ollama narration and TabPFN re-activated.
